title: Thinking Map: the idea-to-plan loop
userRequest: .codeyam/tmp/terminal-drops/e2e91620-546b-4419-80e3-f29ec586415a-image.png I also shared and .md file with the dsign system and have a project scope
description:
Built Thinking Map from an empty repository: an AI thinking partner that deconstructs a vague idea into questions, grows a visual map beside the conversation, grounds it in live web research, absorbs a change of direction without losing the original idea, and ends with what you know, what you don't, three directions and five concrete next steps - with the conversation still open beneath the plan. Next.js + Prisma + SQLite over three tables (ThinkingMap, Message, MapNode, a tree via nullable parentId), with a second front door: an MCP server exposing six tools over the same mapStore on both HTTP and stdio, verified live end to end. 67 scenarios (11 application, 56 component across all 27 components), 103 tests, 62 glossary entries, audit clean.

SCOPE VERDICT - 9 of 10 project deliverables DELIVERED: free-text idea capture; deconstructing questions instead of answers; the live growing map; web-grounded research as findings and gaps; direction changes that add without erasing; the know/don't-know/directions/next-steps output; continued discussion after the plan; persistence across sessions; and the MCP server. 1 DEFERRED, confirmed by the user at the plan gate: registering the MCP server inside Claude Desktop, which is machine configuration and a walkthrough rather than code, so it belongs to the assist track - the config snippet is in the README. No deferral was decided by the agent alone.

HONEST CAVEAT on two delivered rows: this environment has no Anthropic API key, so the deconstructing conversation and the live web research are code-complete and demonstrated through seeded scenarios, but have never been exercised against a live model. Both are marked delivered because the code ships; they need ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env.local before a live demo.

Two environment findings worth keeping: Next 16's default Turbopack dev output does not hydrate through the codeyam preview proxy - nothing was interactive until package.json switched to `next dev --webpack`, isolated with a six-line control component. And a flexbox `min-width: auto` default made the map panel clip its overflow instead of scrolling, which only the deliberately oversized sprawling scenario exposed.
